author: Tana French
introFa: کتاب «In the Woods» نوشته Tana French یکی از منابع ارزشمند و معتبر برای یادگیری زبان انگلیسی در سطح C1 است. این اثر با ساختاری منسجم و غنی، شما را در تسلط بر واژگان و درک مطلب یاری می‌کند.
readingTipsFa: پیش از مطالعه هر بخش از کتاب «In the Woods»، نگاهی سریع به تیترها و ساختار آن بیندازید.
واژگان و اصطلاحات جدید را در زمینه و بافت جمله یادداشت کنید تا در حافظه بلندمدت تثبیت شوند.
پس از پایان هر فصل، نکات کلیدی و آموخته‌های خود را مرور کرده و به زبان خود خلاصه کنید.

content: LANGUAGE IO63 language shun, this book fills a great need. Colloquialisms, though, like / expect you're right, {weeks) on end and proverbs {It's the last straw . ..) are, to most of us, a constituent part of the standard language; we would not wish, nor do we need, to turn to a specialist dictionary to find them. Listing/>z'c& on, pick up, etc. separately from pick makes for easy reference and keeps entries short. Grammatical information is minimal. Verbs, tran- sitive or intransitive, are indicated only by {to), and not enough help is given with constructions, e.g. voir du mime ceil for to see eye to eye {with s.o.). Context markers are few: U.S. for most Americanisms, though not, e.g., figure; langage enfantin for the odd baby-word, e.g. moo-cow, but not doggy, etc.; d'unefemme for appropriate sex words. The obsolete, regional or dialectal is rarely indicated, e.g. flapper, whacker, owtfor nowt. Each word or sense is labelled either F: = familiar; colloquial, P: = popular; slang, V: = vulgar or VV: = very vulgar; 'taboo*. Such distinctions are of necessity subjective, but there are anomalies, e.g. fist. . . Phut fistful. . . F;fleabag . . . P followed soon by flesh-peddler ... F. Are not P: finger artist, V: to finger oneself and finger-job . . . VV equally vulgar? Why distinguish between V and VV? No word is taboo in every situation, or it would not exist, while any word labelled V is taboo in some circles. Nothing informs the user whether the head-word exists only in slang, e.g. abdabs, or in the standard language too, e.g. jug. 'Nouns have normally been taken as key-words,' the compilers claim, so why enter to be an early bird under early, cold feet under cold, etc.? Different senses of a word are not listed in any consistent order, but this is no great inconvenience, as polysemy seems less rampant in slang than in the standard language. Perfect slang equivalents are rarely provided, as they rarely exist. The compilers have tried to solve this difficult problem reasonably by giving first a translation or paraphrase in Standard French, and then a number of approximate synonyms in slang. The S.F. translations usually convey the sense accurately, though sauter auxyeux will not do for to see with half an eye. Regrettably, the S.F. does not come first in some entries, e.g. show-off; in many there is more than one S.F. version, e.g. egghead', sometimes the slang version comes between two S.F. versions, e.g. to keep one's end up. This lack of system makes it difficult for English users to know what is slang and what is not. Too many slang versions may confuse the issue. Monter sur ses grands chevaux translates to get on {ride) one's high horse, but is offered too frequently. More importantly, slang versions of a different register from the original are inadmissible; capote anglaise is acceptable for French letter . . . F, used, if rather apologetically, in family planning literature, where I foresee no future for impermdable a Popaull Asterisks after S.F. words refer the user to lists of slang synonyms at the end, but what is the use of a list of forty-one slang terms for femme which does not distinguish the admiring from the contemptuous, the lecherous from the sexist? The compilers aimed 'to help English speakers to find the French equiva- lents of current words and expressions in non-standard English', but their lack of detail on social and linguistic context will frustrate such users. By SYLVA CLAPIN. (Langue Francaise au Quebec, 2). Quebec: Presses dePUniversitS Laval. 1974. xlvi-f 388 pp. S12.00. Le Parler populaire des Canadiens frangais. By NARCISSE-EUTROPE DIONNE. (Langue Francaise au Quebec, 3). Quebec: Presses de l'Universite Laval. 1974. xxiv + 671 pp. $16.00. Apres le Glossaire du Parler frangais au Canada, reedite en 1968 dans la section «Lexicologie et lexicographie» de la collection «Langue francaise au Quebec), voici que paraissent en reproduction mecanique deux des lexiques quebecois les plus importants de la fin du XIXe siecle et du debut du XXe, le premier publie d'abord en 1894 (reimprime en 1902), le second en 1909, l'un et l'autre devenus depuis longtemps introuvables. L'avant-propos de Georges Straka, que reproduisent les deux volumes, explique clairement le sens et fournit les raisons, avec de nombreux exemples a l'appui, des pre- sentes renditions. En fait, dans l'attente forcement patiente de l'oeuvre repondant en tous points aux exigences scientifiques actuelles que doit etre le futur Tresor de la langue frangaise au Quibec, dont la parution n'est pas pour demain, et meme alors! les travaux de Clapin et de Dionne, souvent plus complets et apportant maintes fois des eclaircissements plus abondants et plus precis que le Glossaire, continueront d'interesser et de renseigner les chercheurs et les amateurs. Chacun selon son caractere particulier — Clapin, par exemple, fait etat d'un «besoin d'agression» contre les puristes —, ils gardent l'un et l'autre leur «valeur documentaire en tant que recueils de mots et de significations*. On se devait de les reproduire tels quels, puisque, aussi bien, comme le Glossaire, l'un et l'autre «est un document, un temoin de son temps, et a un document on ne touche pas, on le respecte». UNIVERSITY D'OTTAWA REJEAN ROBIDOUX Dictionnaire de la linguistique. By GEORGES MOUNIN. Paris: Presses Univer- sitaires de France. 1974. xxxix + 399 pp. The authors of this dictionary have rather 'missed the bus', since no less than three similar works were published in France in 1973. This one was produced under the direction of Mounin by a team of nineteen people, mainly postgraduates and junior university staff.
